subject.title: Feature: Multi-index embedding memory with model-aware failover (no mixed vector spaces)

question: Should OpenClaw adopt first-class per-model memory indexes for safe embedding failover now, and should that contract live in memory-core, a plugin API extension, or an external memory plugin?
rationale: The requested behavior adds config surface, persistent schema/index identity, ingestion coordination, provider-routing policy, observability, and migration/doctor requirements, so automation should not choose the product boundary.

options.title: Design the memory-core/API contract first
options.body: Keep this issue open and have the memory owner define the multi-index config, storage, migration, status, and plugin boundary before implementation.

options.title: Route to plugin API or external plugin
options.body: If maintainers want this outside bundled memory-core, define the missing plugin seam and let an external memory plugin own multi-index failover.

options.title: Defer broad failover
options.body: Keep the existing identity guard and only repair narrower provider recovery bugs such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/96534 for now.

recommendation.title: Design the memory-core/API contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and have the memory owner define the multi-index config, storage, migration, status, and plugin boundary before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: osolmaz is the live assignee and has recent memory embedding provider-boundary history, making him the best available owner for the product/API choice.
